newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil steady on China demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil steady on China demand.

text.p: Asian gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Monday despite the lower than expected Indian diesel purchase for January, as the market looked to China for support, traders said.

December gas oil swaps were last quoted at $30.50/$30.70, largely unchanged from Friday in quiet trade. January traded earlier on Monday at $29.90 per barrel, unchanged from Friday levels, brokers said.
"The IOC (Indian Oil Corp) award is bearish but China is buying," one trader said.

India bought in a tender a modest 255,000-tonnes of diesel for delivery in January down from initial expectations of 700,000 tonnes and also lower than the late Friday expectations of 350,000 tonnes, brokers said.

Traders said the market was supported by tight December supplies from regional sources. As a result, Chinese buyers are paying up to $249 a tonne for small lots sold on an ex-terminal basis in Hong Kong.
Offers to China for cargoes are at around $239 a tonne cost-and freight South China with firm bids about $3-$4 less, traders said.
Physical gas oil in Singapore was bid on Friday to a new five-year of $31.00 a barrel free-on-board. Sellers were sidelined because of tight prompt supplies, traders said.
The jet fuel market remained firm on winter demand from North Asia as cold weather finally sets in, traders said.
In the Singapore physical market, a bid by a major for 120,000-barrels at $32.30 a barrel fob, up 35 cents from Thursday's traded post-winter high, failed to find sellers.
The December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) rose early Monday and bids were quoted at $1.90 a barrel up from Friday's $1.80 bid, brokers said.

Naphtha was talked weaker with crude in very quiet trade. December was last bid at $23.30 with no firm sellers seen, brokers said, from Friday's $23.55/$23.70. Fuel oil opened firm on tight regional supplies and Chinese buying interest. December was notionally quoted at $119.75/$121.00 a tonne, largely unchanged from Friday.
